title: Evaluate confirmation results — Harlow Instruments
instructions: You sent positive confirmations of December 31 receivable balances for Harlow Instruments. Select the most appropriate response to each result.

exhibits.title: Confirmation results
exhibits.content:
| Customer | Result |
|---|---|
| Adler | Confirms the balance without exception. |
| Benning | Says $18,000 of the balance is for goods it hadn't received at December 31. Harlow's shipping log shows the goods left the dock on January 3; the sale was recorded December 30. |
| Carver | Says it mailed a $9,500 check on December 30. Harlow recorded the receipt on January 4. |
| Dorsey | No response after a second request. |
| Ellison | Disputes $12,000, saying the goods arrived damaged and a credit was promised. |
| Fenwick | Confirms the balance, but the reply came from a free personal email address rather than Fenwick's corporate domain. |

parts.prompt: Select the response for each confirmation.

rows.label: Adler
options: No further action needed
Timing difference — verify the subsequent receipt
Cutoff error — propose an adjustment
Investigate the dispute and evaluate the allowance
Perform alternative procedures
Assess the reliability of the response before relying on it
rows.explanation: An agreed confirmation is sufficient evidence for that balance.

rows.label: Benning
options: No further action needed
Timing difference — verify the subsequent receipt
Cutoff error — propose an adjustment
Investigate the dispute and evaluate the allowance
Perform alternative procedures
Assess the reliability of the response before relying on it
rows.explanation: Goods shipped January 3 were billed December 30: revenue and receivables are overstated at year-end.

rows.label: Carver
options: No further action needed
Timing difference — verify the subsequent receipt
Cutoff error — propose an adjustment
Investigate the dispute and evaluate the allowance
Perform alternative procedures
Assess the reliability of the response before relying on it
rows.answer: Timing difference — verify the subsequent receipt
rows.explanation: A payment in transit is a timing difference; verify it by tracing to the January deposit.

rows.label: Dorsey
options: No further action needed
Timing difference — verify the subsequent receipt
Cutoff error — propose an adjustment
Investigate the dispute and evaluate the allowance
Perform alternative procedures
Assess the reliability of the response before relying on it
rows.explanation: For a nonresponse to a positive confirmation, examine subsequent cash receipts, shipping documents and invoices.

rows.label: Ellison
options: No further action needed
Timing difference — verify the subsequent receipt
Cutoff error — propose an adjustment
Investigate the dispute and evaluate the allowance
Perform alternative procedures
Assess the reliability of the response before relying on it
rows.answer: Investigate the dispute and evaluate the allowance
rows.explanation: A disputed amount may require a credit memo or an allowance; investigate with sales and returns records.

rows.label: Fenwick
options: No further action needed
Timing difference — verify the subsequent receipt
Cutoff error — propose an adjustment
Investigate the dispute and evaluate the allowance
Perform alternative procedures
Assess the reliability of the response before relying on it
rows.answer: Assess the reliability of the response before relying on it
rows.explanation: A reply from an unexpected source raises doubts about its reliability; verify it, for example by contacting the customer directly.
